# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–11 (Complete – Updated 98)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; spring of second year; summer of second year; autumn of second year; winter of second year; spring of third year (auction, financial crisis, engagement rupture); military mobilization period following Napoleon's escape and landing; thaw period with frost-silvered hedges and rain threatening, early light of year; summer of third year; evening with wind off water, salt and tar smell, frost silvering hedges overnight, vespers bells, bees in lavender; early autumn with coughing sickness, dog barking, turnips on cart, river up, price of salt concerns; late April: gusty raw day with rain whipping pavement, end of day with early light, smoke flat over fields; church service with rattling rain on windows; autumn of third year (river crossing at Quenwick); Brighton period following George-Amelia marriage (early spring/late April): turnips on cart, threatening rain, wind off water with salt and tar smell, frost-silvered hedges, flat smoke over fields, ruts and puddles after thaw; Dobbin's delayed arrival bringing news of Belgium orders; early light of year returning; **current: Dobbin in London conducting campaign with Osborne family before confronting father; frost has silvered hedges overnight**
- **Primary Locations**: [All previous locations plus] **Brighton** (George-Amelia honeymoon, Rawdon-Rebecca residence, Jos Sedley's visit); Miremere and Quenwick (settlements by Breena Orlwood, Pebin Wexwood); Chatham (embarkation point for Belgium); Belgium (destination of army deployment); **London** (current: Dobbin's campaign with Osborne sisters); Cheltenham, Chowringhee, Calcutta (Jos's references)

## Main Characters

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca Rawdon Crawley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Age nineteen; father artist/drawing teacher; mother French opera-girl; small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large attractive eyes; skilled musician, linguist, artist; talented mimic
- **Marriage**: Secretly married to Captain Rawdon Crawley in City church; living with him at Brighton in "very best apartments at the inn"
- **Financial Situation**: Dunned by creditors; bailiffs watched greengrocer's opposite last week; relies on Miss Crawley's relenting for relief
- **Talents**: Adroit treatment of duns; remarkable ability to talk creditors over; practice began immediately after marriage; husband finds "immense value of such a wife"
- **Current Status**: At Brighton with Rawdon; following Miss Crawley to secure her favor; meeting constantly with George and Amelia Osborne; socializing

**Captain Rawdon Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Captain in Life Guards; celebrated "blood"/dandy; expert boxer, rat-hunter, four-in-hand driver; large, six feet high; generous; over head and ears in debt
- **Marriage**: Secretly married to Rebecca; at Brighton in "very best apartments at the inn"
- **Financial Status**: Bills in abundance; scarcity of ready money; credit in plenty; good spirits despite debt; long custom, manly appearance, faultless boots serve him well; all hopes depend on Miss Crawley's relenting
- **Recent Activity**: Jos Sedley played billiards with him at Brighton, replenishing his purse with ready money

**Miss Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Inherited large fortune; silly, romantic; very attached to Rawdon
- **Response to Marriage**: Fainted and suffered hysterics; confined to bed; letters unopened; not recovering from shock
- **Current Status**: At Brighton; holding out against Rawdon and Rebecca's attempts; refuses entry; emissaries continually planted at her door

**Mrs. Bute Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Sister-in-law to Miss Crawley; positioned as nurse; continuously present; cultivates staff loyalty; takes Miss Crawley on diversionary drives; tells stories against Rawdon and Rebecca

**Amelia Osborne (Mrs. George Osborne)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Small, modest, unaffected; tender heart; timid; sweet modest soul
- **Status - MARRIED**: Married to George Osborne in chapel near Fulham Road, late April; dressed in brown silk pelisse, straw bonnet with pink ribbon, white Chantilly lace veil, gold chain and watch (from Dobbin), mother's diamond brooch
- **Honeymoon**: Enjoying "first blushing days" at Brighton with George; happy, rosy, round face; meeting constantly with Rebecca and Rawdon; poor girl who would have died without George's faith; loved by Miss Jane Osborne
- **Emotional State**: Fear overcome by love at marriage; response came "fluttering up to her lips from her heart"

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Handsome; excellent at games; over head and ears in debt; gambler, drunkster, profligate; finest young fellow in regiment; bravest, handsomest officer in army
- **Status - MARRIED**: Married Amelia Osborne late April in chapel near Fulham Road; pale and agitated before ceremony; appeared proud and radiant after; married without father's consent; marriage proceeded because George could not give up Amelia; holds engagement as most sacred duty
- **Honeymoon**: At Brighton with Amelia enjoying "first blushing days"; expressed delight at Dobbin's arrival; received news of Belgium orders; anxious about father's reaction; currently abroad (at Brighton)
- **Military Orders**: Received news that army ordered to Belgium; all guards embark from Chatham next week
- **Relationship with Father**: Financial rupture imminent; John Osborne opposed marriage; George trembles for father's reaction; banters Dobbin about Miss Jane Osborne, saying "Hang it, Will, why don't you take old Jane? She'll have you if you ask her"

**Captain William Dobbin** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Role in Marriage**: Primary architect of reconciliation between George and Amelia; convinced both to proceed; urged George to act before regiment's orders; presented gold chain and watch to Amelia; groomsman
- **Emotional State Post-Marriage**: Felt miserable and lonely after ceremony; left in reverie without celebration; longed heart-sick for first days to be over to see her again
- **Current Campaign**: Before confronting John Osborne, executing Machiavellian strategy to make friends of rest of Osborne family, particularly the ladies; believes women cannot be angry at romantic marriage
- **Strategy Execution**: 
  - Made inquiry regarding mother's social engagements; found parties where Misses Osborne would be present
  - Attended ball despite abhorrence of routs and evening parties; danced with both Misses Osborne; was "prodigiously polite"
  - Asked Miss Jane Osborne for conversation next day, saying he had news of "very greatest interest"
  - During meeting with Miss Jane: found her violently agitated at his request; when she started back, made as if to faint, then became composed; they sat in silence while Sacrifice of Iphigenia clock ticked audibly
  - Spoke of dangers to soldiers, praised George as "finest young fellow in regiment," called Amelia charming and worthy of affection
  - Eventually revealed George's marriage to Amelia; related circumstances: George could not give up Amelia (poor girl would have died without his faith); Old Sedley refused consent; license obtained; Jos Sedley gave away bride; honeymoon at Brighton in Jos's chariot-and-four
  - Asked Miss Jane to befriend Amelia and George with their father; asked permission to call again (readily granted); correctly conjectured news would be told to other ladies within five minutes
- **Belief**: George having often bantered him gracefully about taking "old Jane"; Dobbin "not altogether unconscious of the state of affairs" regarding Miss Jane Osborne's feelings toward him

**Jane Osborne (Miss Osborne)** [CHARACTER]
- Young woman; fair; unmarried spinster; tender heart; capable of generous forgiveness
- **Feelings toward George**: Sister who loves him; originally expected his return and full reconciliation with father; believed "Woman forgives but too readily"
- **Response to Dobbin's News**: Violently agitated at his request for conversation; started back, gazed on him and ground, nearly fainted (Dobbin treading on her toes brought her to self-control); during conversation, felt pressure of hand when Dobbin asked if she would give him up if poor; thought she would faint when Dobbin revealed marriage but gathered composure; moved by his words about Amelia's faithful heart and suffering; shocked by news but capable of defending George; acknowledged feeling for Amelia but expressed father would never consent; argued George must give up Amelia; responded to Dobbin's counter-argument about man giving up woman he loved when misfortune befell her; had hand extended to Dobbin when he made adroit question; now knows George is married to Amelia; will likely report news to other Osborne family members within five minutes

**Maria Osborne** [CHARACTER]
- Sister to Jane and George; present during Dobbin-Jane conversation; laughed with Miss Wirt at Jane's discomfiture over Dobbin's mention of "George"; will learn of George's marriage from Jane within five minutes

**Miss Wirt** [CHARACTER]
- Companion or relation to Osborne family; left drawing room to fetch Maria; laughed at Jane's discomfiture; present during news distribution

**John Osborne (Old Mr. Osborne)** [CHARACTER]
- Wealthy merchant; George's father; savage, determined man
- **Status**: George married Amelia despite father's opposition; refused to give consent to match; offered George superb establishment that was refused; financial rupture imminent; Dobbin has not yet confronted him; approaching confrontation pending; George trembles for father's reaction

**Other Characters**: John Sedley (ruined, bankrupt), Mrs. Sedley (Amelia's mother, faithful consoler), Jos Sedley (splendid appearance, fatter than ever, at Brighton, billiards player)

## Critical Facts and Status (Updated)

- **GEORGE-AMELIA MARRIAGE - COMPLETED AND HONEYMOON ONGOING**: Married late April in chapel near Fulham Road; enjoying honeymoon at Brighton; George married Amelia without father's consent because he could not give her up; Amelia poor girl who would have died without his faith
- **DOBBIN'S STRATEGIC CAMPAIGN - IN PROGRESS**: Before confronting John Osborne, conducting Machiavellian campaign to secure family's support (particularly the ladies); has successfully made contact with Miss Jane Osborne; revealed George's marriage to her; tactfully explained circumstances and George's faithful love; secured her sympathy for Amelia; obtained permission to call again; believes news will reach other family members within five minutes; Miss Jane was deeply affected but believes father will never consent; Dobbin working to have ladies on his side before final confrontation with old Mr. Osborne
- **MISS JANE OSBORNE'S FEELINGS - REVEALED**: George has bantered Dobbin about her, saying she'll have him if he asks (five-to-two odds); Dobbin "not altogether unconscious of the state of affairs"; she became violently agitated when he requested conversation; nearly fainted at his mention of George; appeared to feel pressure of hand when Dobbin asked if she would give him up if poor; tender-hearted and capable of forgiveness; believed to have affection for Dobbin (George's jest suggesting she would accept him)
- **FINANCIAL CRISIS ONGOING**: Rawdon and Rebecca still dunned by creditors; rely on Miss Crawley's relenting; Jos temporarily replenished Rawdon's purse via billiards; Miss Crawley still holding out against them at Brighton
- **MILITARY ORDERS PENDING**: Army ordered to Belgium to pursue Napoleon; embarkation from Chatham imminent (next week); regiment mobilization urgent; Dobbin aware orders may come "at a day's warning"
- **FAMILY COMMUNICATION STRATEGY**: Dobbin correctly predicted Miss Jane would tell other ladies (Maria and Miss Wirt) immediately; strategy to divide family support before John Osborne confrontation underway
